title: Hardware Failure Simulation and Tenant Resilience Acceptance Test Harness
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook defines a reproducible, operator-run test harness used during private deployment acceptance, operator certification, and post-installation hardening to validate tenant-level resilience against realistic hardware failure modes. The goals are to: ensure tenant SLA preservation, validate failover & eviction behavior, and collect forensic evidence suitable for customer acceptance reports.

Scope and audience

- Scope: private VPC and on-prem Redwood Private installations (single-region and multi-zone control plane). This covers GPU hosts, local NVMe, network fabric, and control-plane nodes involved in serving runtime.
- Audience: field operators, SREs, platform engineers, and customer technical owners during onboarding.

Why this harness exists

Private deployments operate at tenant scale with heterogeneous hardware and strict SLA contracts. Component-level chaos testing in the lab is insufficient — we must exercise tenant-level failure and recovery patterns in a controlled operator-run harness that mirrors production tenant traffic, KV cache state, and artifact refresh cycles. This document provides: harness components, test scenarios, acceptance criteria, observability checks, and post-test evidence packaging for customers.

Test harness components

1) Workload generator (tenant-representative):
   - Light-weight synthetic traffic that reproduces typical sequence-length distribution, prefix repetition, and burst patterns for the tenant.
   - Supports replay of recorded production traces (anonymized) and parameterized synthetic workloads.

2) Fault injector:
   - Controller that can safely remove power to a GPU host (simulated via hypervisor pause or IPMI if hardware access allowed), throttle NIC bandwidth, or corrupt an NVMe device at the block layer (non-destructive mode).

3) Orchestration state harness:
   - Scripts to snapshot runtime KV caches, connection tables, and model artifact pointers before fault injection; and record post-failure reconciliation steps.

4) Observability capture:
   - Centralized collector that captures: per-tenant request latency/percentiles, per-token CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit-rate timeline, model load events, container kill traces, systemd/journald logs, and pprof traces where available.

5) Evidence packager:
   - Automated tool to produce a customer-facing artifact bundle: test timeline, raw traces, curated charts, and a signed operator runbook describing actions taken and any divergence from the canonical protocol.

Environment and preconditions

- Operator privileges: operator account with documented escrowing of credentials and RBAC scoped just for the test window.
- Canary tenant: a tenant configured with the same resource profile and traffic shape as the target customer. No customer data in test tenant.
- Baseline run: run workload generator for 30–60 minutes to capture baseline performance and KV cache warmup state.
- Backup snapshot: create runtime and orchestration snapshots (artifact manifests, KV cache digests, and routing tables).

Minimum environment requirements table

| Component | Minimum config for harness | Purpose |
|---|---:|---|
| GPU hosts under test | 2 availability fault domains, at least 1 host with spare capacity | Validate host failover and tenant affinity changes |
| Control plane nodes | 3-node control plane or equivalent HA control plane | Validate failover of control-plane role elections |
| Telemetry retention | 1h high-resolution + 7d aggregated | Capture pre/post failure traces and trends |
| Network emulator | Rate limiter capable of 10 Gbps shaping | Simulate partial NIC failures and bandwidth storms |
| Storage emulator | NVMe fault-inject with read-only fail mode | Validate model artifact fallback and rehydrate behavior |

Test scenarios (operator-run)

Each scenario has: objective, preconditions, steps, expected behavior, and evidence artifacts. Scenarios are ordered to increase impact; stop the run if acceptance criteria fail at any critical step.

Scenario A: Single GPU host hard failure (non-corrupting)
- Objective: Validate tenant traffic reroute and model hot-swap without token loss above SLO.
- Preconditions: Baseline run complete; KV cache warm.
- Steps:
  1. Trigger workload generator at nominal peak (65–80% of baseline max).
  2. Wait 5 minutes to ensure steady-state.
  3. Use fault injector to remove host (power-off or hypervisor pause).
  4. Monitor routing events, per-tenant latency, and request failures.
  5. After 3 minutes observe, bring host back and record rejoin timeline.
- Expected behavior:
  - 99th percentile latency increase <= 2x baseline for no more than 90 seconds.
  - Successful requests >= 99.5% during window (adjustable by customer SLA).
  - KV cache miss spike followed by rewarming under 5 minutes using warm-start strategy.
- Evidence:
  - Timeline of host removal and rejoin, request logs, injected fault record, and KV cache hit-rate plot.

Scenario B: Partial NIC bandwidth degradation (throttling)
- Objective: Validate graceful degradation, backpressure propagation, and operator-initiated traffic-shedding behavior.
- Steps:
  1. Start workload at 90% of saturation to make degradation observable.
  2. Throttle NIC bandwidth to 20% on a subset of serving hosts for 4 minutes.
  3. Observe fallback routing, any request requeues, and autoscaler decisions.
- Expected behavior:
  - Traffic is routed away from impacted hosts within 30s of sustained packet loss.
  - No data corruption; in-flight requests may be retried with idempotency guarantees.
- Evidence: network packet capture snippet, routing events, autoscaler logs.

Scenario C: NVMe transient error during model load
- Objective: Confirm artifact fetch fallback to remote store and successful model rehydrate with minimal request disruption.
- Steps:
  1. Introduce transient read errors on NVMe device used for model caches (non-destructive).
  2. Trigger model swap on impacted host (simulate model refresh event).
  3. Observe artifact fetch paths and monitor model load latencies.
- Expected behavior: fetch falls back to remote artifact store within configured 15s and model load completes with a 95th percentile < 30s.
- Evidence: block device error logs, artifact-fetch traces, rehydrate success event.

Acceptance criteria and SLO mapping

- Critical acceptance criteria (must pass):
  - Customer-facing request success rate >= customer SLA (default 99.5%) across scenario windows.
  - No silent data corruption (cross-verify request hashes where applicable).
  - Operator-run evidence bundle includes baseline, fault injector input, telemetry captures, and signed operator checklist.

- Non-critical (informative) metrics captured:
  - KV cache warmup time, model load latency distribution, CPU/GPU tail utilization changes, and spool-failure rates.

Runbook: operator checklist (pre, during, post)

Pre-run (operator)
1) Confirm operator window and customer communications templates are in place.
2) Snapshot orchestration manifests and artifact digests.
3) Ensure canary tenant is isolated and synthetic traffic contains no PII.
4) Verify telemetry and evidence storage has >= 2x expected test volume headroom.

During run
1) One operator is primary controller; a second operator monitors telemetry.
2) Record timestamps for each action and sign the running checklist.
3) If critical acceptance criteria are breached, abort further scenarios and execute the immediate remediation checklist.

Post-run and evidence packaging
1) Gather all traces, produce canonical charts (latency percentiles, hit-rates, host events).
2) Run automated integrity checks against request logs for any anomalies.
3) Produce evidence bundle containing: README, operator checklist, raw and aggregated telemetry, and a short executive summary with bullet conclusions.
4) Deliver bundle to customer per evidence delivery contract and update customer onboarding record.

Remediation paths and rollback notes

- If a test uncovers an unrecoverable defect in artifact handling or stateful migration, follow the private-deploy forensic rollback protocol (see related pages). Always preserve raw telemetry and avoid destructive corrective actions until forensic snapshot is captured.

Reporting template for customers

- Executive summary (1 page): scope, outcome (pass/fail), high-level impact to SLA, mitigation taken.
- Technical appendix: timelines, charts, and raw trace references.
- Action items: prioritized list with owner and ETA for fixes.

Ownership and scheduling

- Owner: eng-private-deployments / Day-2 Operations (primary: Asha Patel).
- Certification gate: operator must run full harness successfully twice in a staging environment before field runs on customer production hardware.
- Frequency: recommended quarterly or prior to any major runtime or firmware upgrade.

References and related artifacts

- Use the artifact manifests described in the operator-privileged artifact-schema-migration contracts when capturing model pointers.
- Cross-reference the tenant-eviction-and-safe-state-sanitization-playbook for tenant cleanup steps after high-impact runs.

Appendix: run parameters (example CLI)

- Example command to start a synthetic workload replay:
  redwood-testctl workload replay --tenant canary-123 --trace-file traces/canary-traffic-2026-02-10.json --qps 400 --seq-dist skewed --duration 00:45:00

- Example fault-inject invocation (nic throttle):
  redwood-faultctl nic throttle --host host-34 --percent 20 --duration 00:04:00 --evidence-id ev-20260212-34

Notes and caveats

- Never run this harness on a customer tenant containing production data. Always use an isolated canary tenant and obtain written sign-off for the operator window.
- Some hardware vendors do not permit destructive block fault injection in the field; in those cases use hypervisor-level simulations and vendor-provided diagnostics.
